questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-1,{x}_{3}=3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-1$ and ${x}_{3}=3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =2(x-(-1))(x-(-1))(x-3) \\  & =2(x+1)(x+1)(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+1)(x+1)(x-3) & =2({x}^{2}+2x+1)(x-3) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}-6x+x-3) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-5x-3) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x-6.$

questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-2.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{1}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-2(x-(-5))(x-0)(x-1) \\  & =-2x(x+5)(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x(x+5)(x-1) & =-2x({x}^{2}+4x-5) \\  & =-2({x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-5x) \\  & =-2{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+10x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-2{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+10x.$

questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-3,{x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $5.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-3$ and ${x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=5,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =5(x-(-3))(x-(-3))(x-1) \\  & =5(x+3)(x+3)(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5(x+3)(x+3)(x-1) & =5({x}^{2}+6x+9)(x-1) \\  & =5({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+6{x}^{2}-6x+9x-9) \\  & =5({x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}+3x-9) \\  & =5{x}^{3}+25{x}^{2}+15x-45.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=5{x}^{3}+25{x}^{2}+15x-45.$

questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-3,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $P(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our cubic equation has roots ${x}_{1}=-3,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =2(x-(-3))(x-0)(x-5) \\  & =2x(x+3)(x-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2x(x+3)(x-5) & =2x({x}^{2}-2x-15) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-15x) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-30x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-30x.$

questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-2,{x}_{2,3}=3\pm \text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-1.$ Find $f(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2,3}=3\pm \text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =-1(x-(-2))(x-(3+\text{i}))(x-(3-\text{i})) \\  & =-(x+2)(x-(3+\text{i}))(x-(3-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x+2)(x-(3+\text{i}))(x-(3-\text{i})) & = \\ -(x+2)({x}^{2}-x(3-\text{i})-x(3+\text{i})+(3+\text{i})(3-\text{i})) & = \\ -(x+2)({x}^{2}-6x+10) & = \\ -({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+10x+2{x}^{2}-12x+20) & = \\ -{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+2x-20 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=-{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+2x-20.$

questions.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2,3}=1\pm 2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=6,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =6(x-3)(x-(1+2\text{i}))(x-(1-2\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}6(x-3)(x-(1+2\text{i}))(x-(1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 6(x-3)({x}^{2}-x(1+2\text{i})-x(1-2\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 6(x-3)({x}^{2}-2x+5) & = \\ 6({x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}+11x-15) & = \\ 6{x}^{3}-30{x}^{2}+66x-90.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: The cubic polynomial $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-1,{x}_{2,3}=\pm 4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $f(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2,3}=\pm 4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =2(x-(-1))(x-4\text{i})(x-(-4\text{i})) \\  & =2(x+1)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+1)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i}) & = \\ 2(x+1)({x}^{2}-(4\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ 2(x+1)({x}^{2}+16) & = \\ 2({x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+16x+16) & = \\ 2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+32x+32 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+32x+32.$

Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $1.$
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2,3}=\pm 3\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=1.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =1(x-4)(x-3\text{i})(x-(-3\text{i})) \\  & =(x-4)(x-3\text{i})(x+3\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)(x-3\text{i})(x+3\text{i}) & = \\ (x-4)({x}^{2}-x(-3\text{i})-x(3\text{i})+(3\text{i})(-3\text{i})) & = \\ (x-4)({x}^{2}+9) & = \\ {x}^{3}+9x-4{x}^{2}-36 & = \\ {x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+9x-36 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)={x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+9x-36.$

canonical_examples.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots $x_1=x_2=2,x_3=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $3.$ Find $P(x).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${\color{black}x_1=x_2=2}$ and ${\color{black}x_3=1},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is ${\color{black}a=3},$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =3(x-2)(x-2)(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x-2)(x-2)(x-1) & =3({x}^{2}-4x+4)(x-1) \\  & =3({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}+4x+4x-4) \\  & =3({x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}+8x-4) \\  & =3{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}+24x-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x) = 3x^3 -15x^2+24x-12.$
